newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MTBE edges up as outlook remains bullish.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MTBE edges up as outlook remains bullish.

text.p: U.S. spot MTBE prices edged upward this week as the outlook remained bullish amid solid demand from refiners and production that is pinched by a number of maintenance projects now underway, traders said.

Record production of gasoline in recent weeks has included high reformulated gasoline (RFG) production and thus implicated MTBE, which is enjoying the demand of nearly 300,000 barrels per day (bpd) -- levels not seen since the eve of RFG's January 1995 launch in the smoggiest U.S. cities.
"The high gasoline production may be bearish for gasoline, but it's bullish for MTBE," said one trader.

Indeed the price differential between spot MTBE in Houston and nearby gasoline futures on NYMEX has expanded in the last week by nearly 2.00 cents a gallon to over 24 cents, mostly due to futures declines but also due to MTBE's modest gains.
MTBE's advance has been been helped by production issues, notably turnaroud activity going on at an ARCO Chemical plant in the Netherlands and by work at an MTBE plant in Venezuela.

Traders and analysts have been predicting a drop in imports this month into NYH partly due to turnaround at Arco's Rotterdam facility and to the catalyst change at the 12,500 barrel per day Jose, Venezuela plant that will be out until June 28.
"Arco is on turnaround and we will not be seeing that material for probably all of June," said Bill Richards of DeWitt & Co.

Offers on prompt material in Houston nudged up by about 0.50 cent to 81 cents a gallon, with bids holding steady at 80 cents. Deals were getting done this week in that range, traders said. Backwardation reflected the tight supplies, with barrels for first-half July delivery pegged at between 79 and 80 cents a gallon.

The 'up-down' Houston-New York differential stood in a fairly balanced +3.75/+4.00 cents over range, with prompt deals heard done 84.50 cents a gallon, and at 82.50, which some players considered below market.
-- Oliver Ludwig New York Oil Desk 1 212 859 1633
